Fix https://github.com/VirtusLab/orca/issues/194: Worktree tests fail on macOS because /var is a symlink to /private/var

On macOS, 12 worktree tests fail, all with the same shape: the expected path starts with `/var/...` and the obtained one with `/private/var/...`.

```
=> Diff (- expected, + obtained)
 Some(
-  value = /var/folders/.../T/orca-gitrepo-3149900318845979999/.orca/worktrees/cebfb101fb50
+  value = /private/var/folders/.../T/orca-gitrepo-3149900318845979999/.orca/worktrees/cebfb101fb50
 )
```

Failing tests (macOS, `sbt test`):
- `orca.tools.WorktreesTest`: "add creates a worktree that list then reports", "mainCheckout answers the same path from the repo and its worktree", "mainCheckout answers the checkout when the git dir lives outside it", "mainCheckoutOrReason separates a non-repository from a bad layout"
- `orca.runner.WorktreeRunTest`: "the worktree lives under .orca/worktrees, keyed by the task text", "re-resolving the same task text reuses the worktree already there", "recreating one worktree leaves the repository's others registered"
- `orca.runner.FlowLifecycleTest`: "--worktree: the run happens in the worktree, the invoking checkout is untouched, and a re-run returns to it"
- `orca.shell.WorktreeScanTest`: "an orca worktree is scanned alongside the checkout", "a worktree does not scan its siblings", "worktrees are ranked by when each last recorded a run", "only the most recently used worktrees are scanned, up to the cap"

## Cause

On macOS the temp directory lives under `/var/folders/...`, and `/var` is a symlink to `/private/var`. Fixtures build their expected paths from the temp directory as given (`TempDirs.dir`, used by `GitRepo.empty`/`seeded`). The code under test reports paths as git resolves them, e.g. `git worktree list`, which prints resolved paths. The two name the same directory but compare unequal. CI's Linux runners have no symlink in the temp path, so CI passes.

`FlowLifecycleTest`'s `--worktree` test was hidden behind #190's `NoClassDefFoundError` until that was fixed.

## Fix

Make the fixture return a resolved path, e.g. `os.Path(dir.toNIO.toRealPath())`, in `TempDirs.dir`. Every fixture builds on it, so the expected paths would then match what git reports. The alternative is to compare resolved paths in each assertion, but that repeats the fix in 12 places and the next test would miss it.

Before choosing, check whether any production path comparison mixes a user-given path with a git-reported one. Such a comparison would be a real bug on macOS rather than a test-only one: the tests pass a `/var/...` path in, which is what a user's `cwd` under a symlinked directory would look like.
